headline_marked: Iran's IRGC claims [[US military helicopters destroyed]] in Kuwait attack
headline: Iran's IRGC claims US military helicopters destroyed in Kuwait attack
summary: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it targeted the Ali Al-Salem airbase, destroying drone hangars and fuel tanks.
details: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claims to have destroyed several US military helicopters during an attack on the Ali Al-Salem airbase in Kuwait.
According to Fars News Agency, the operation, named 'Operation Nasr-2', was carried out as a response to previous US attacks.
The IRGC further claims that two drone hangars and an aircraft fuel tank were set on fire and destroyed in the strike.
As of now, neither the United States nor Kuwait has issued an official statement regarding these claims.
The actual extent of the damage and losses has not been independently verified by any third party.
This development comes amid heightened military tensions between the US and Iran in the Middle East, with both sides engaging in retaliatory strikes.
caption:
Iran's IRGC claims to have destroyed US military helicopters in Kuwait. Was this a direct response to US strikes?

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claims to have destroyed several US military helicopters during an attack on the Ali Al-Salem airbase in Kuwait.

According to Fars News Agency, the operation, named 'Operation Nasr-2', was carried out as a response to previous US attacks.

The IRGC further claims that two drone hangars and an aircraft fuel tank were set on fire and destroyed in the strike.

As of now, neither the United States nor Kuwait has issued an official statement regarding these claims.

The actual extent of the damage and losses has not been independently verified by any third party.

This development comes amid heightened military tensions between the US and Iran in the Middle East, with both sides engaging in retaliatory strikes.

Source: Jamuna TV

headline_marked: 626 Bangladeshis face [[auto-cancellation of UAE visas]], gov't says
headline: 626 Bangladeshis face auto-cancellation of UAE visas, gov't says
summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid clarifies that only 626 visas were cancelled, debunking reports of  seorang 5,000 people affected.
details: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid announced that 626 Bangladeshis have experienced the 'auto-cancellation' of their UAE visas. This clarification comes after reports circulated that 5,000 Bangladeshis were affected.

Following an emergency inter-ministerial meeting at the Foreign Ministry on Thursday, the Minister stated that the government is already taking action. Out of the affected individuals, the government has already resent 417 visa renewal applications.

State Minister for Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Nurul Huq Nur announced that a hotline will be launched to provide assistance and collect data on those whose visas were cancelled after returning to Bangladesh.

Minister Nurul Huq Nur also urged Bangladeshi workers in the Middle East to refrain from posting about internal crises or issues of their host countries on social media to avoid further complications.
caption:
626 Bangladeshis have had their UAE visas automatically cancelled. The government is now stepping in to help.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid announced that 626 Bangladeshis have experienced the 'auto-cancellation' of their UAE visas. This clarification comes after reports circulated that 5,000 Bangladeshis were affected.

Following an emergency inter-ministerial meeting at the Foreign Ministry on Thursday, the Minister stated that the government is already taking action. Out of the affected individuals, the government has already resent 417 visa renewal applications.

State Minister for Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Nurul Huq Nur announced that a hotline will be launched to provide assistance and collect data on those whose visas were cancelled after returning to Bangladesh.

Minister Nurul Huq Nur also urged Bangladeshi workers in the Middle East to refrain from posting about internal crises or issues of their host countries on social media to avoid further complications.

#UAE #Bangladesh #VisaCancellation #Expatriates #News

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV
